title: US Naval Observatory Astronomical Applications Department, Data Services
what: USNO Sun and Moon times for the study dates
why: US public domain; records copied

title: Iowa Environmental Mesonet (IEM), Iowa State University: ASOS/AWOS archive, NWS text products, Local Storm Reports
what: hourly airport observations near Washington and Phoenix
why: public domain; records copied

title: NOAA-CIRES-DOE 20th Century Reanalysis v3
why: not held (the server refused); ERA5 used instead

title: NASA OMNIWeb solar wind and geomagnetic data
what: hourly solar wind speed, F10.7 and Kp
why: terms unknown: a compilation that carries indices and solar wind data made outside NASA; records not copied; link only

title: GHCN-Daily
why: terms unknown: a US federal compilation that includes observations supplied by foreign, volunteer and other non-federal observers; records not copied. Daily extremes per period only for first-order stations run by US federal agencies; cooperative and volunteer stations: link only

title: WDC for Geomagnetism, Kyoto: geomagnetic indices and observatory data
why: scientific use only, no commercial use of the indices; link only

title: OurAirports open airport data
why: public domain; records copied

title: National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena (NICAP)
what: NICAP case pages for all three studies
why: terms unknown; link only; the dates and hours of the periods come from them

title: Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects (Condon Report), NCAS Internet edition
what: the 1968 University of Colorado study, chapters on the Washington nights
why: copies allowed only whole, unmodified and non-commercial; link only

title: Integrated Global Radiosonde Archive (IGRA)
why: terms unknown: a US federal compilation that includes soundings supplied by foreign and other non-federal services; records not copied. The inversions found in each sounding only for sites run by US federal agencies (Washington National, Tucson); every other site (the UK site for Rendlesham, Flagstaff): link only

title: World Data Centre for Geomagnetism, Edinburgh (BGS), worldwide observatory data
why: scientific use, commercial use only by agreement; link only

title: VizieR catalogue service (CDS Strasbourg)
why: not held; the sky has 16 bright stars

title: Deseret News archive
why: terms unknown, not held; link only

title: Chronicling America (Historic American Newspapers, Library of Congress)
why: rights in each item are left to the user; date, publication and a link to the page only

title: SIMBAD Astronomical Database (CDS Strasbourg)
why: not held

title: GCAT, General Catalog of Artificial Space Objects (J. McDowell)
what: launches dated to the day within the study spans
why: CC BY 4.0; records copied with credit

title: ROSA P, Repository and Open Science Access Portal (US DOT National Transportation Library)
what: the 1953 radar report on the Washington targets: the entries of its Table I and its assessments, as times, places and numbers
why: US public domain; records copied, no text

title: Project BLUE BOOK - Unidentified Flying Objects (US National Archives)
why: not held; link only

title: GFZ Kp and ap geomagnetic indices since 1932
what: Kp, ap, sunspot number and F10.7
why: CC BY 4.0; records copied with credit

title: JPL planetary and lunar ephemerides, NAIF generic SPK kernels (DE440, DE440s)
why: the files may be used by anyone but redistributed only unmodified; the files are not copied; the positions computed from them are given

title: American Stories (Dell Research Harvard): article texts from Chronicling America newspaper scans
why: CC BY 4.0, but no third-party text is reproduced; date, publication and page only

title: Integrated Surface Database (ISD)
why: terms unknown: a US federal compilation that includes observations supplied by foreign and other non-federal services; records not copied. Nearest-station ranges per period are derived only for stations run by US federal agencies (the National Weather Service, the FAA and the US military); every other station (all Rendlesham stations included): link only

title: USGS ANSS Comprehensive Earthquake Catalog (ComCat), FDSN event service
what: earthquakes and other seismic catalogue entries
why: US public domain; records copied

title: JPL Small-Body Database API (SBDB), Solar System Dynamics
why: terms unknown, not held; no comet position computed

title: JPL Horizons ephemeris system
why: terms unknown, not held

title: Royal Observatory, Greenwich - USAF/NOAA Sunspot Data (NASA Marshall Solar Physics)
why: terms unknown: the observations before 1977 were compiled by the Royal Greenwich Observatory; records not copied; link only

title: Newswire (Dell Research Harvard): de-duplicated US newswire articles 1878 to 1977
why: CC BY 4.0, but no third-party text is reproduced; date, dateline, number of papers printing and number of days printed only

title: NOAA SWPC Solar and Geophysical Event Reports
what: daily lists of solar flares and other solar activity
why: US public domain; records copied

title: NSF NCAR Geoscience Data Exchange (GDEX, formerly the Research Data Archive)
what: ERA5 hourly reanalysis at the reference points, with the inversions read from it
why: CC BY 4.0; records copied with credit

title: CelesTrak SATCAT satellite catalogue
why: data freely available, but not marked for copying; records not copied; counts of objects in orbit and of decays per day only
